cards.memory: Data + Compute + Learning = the rise of computer vision.
cards.trap: Classification says WHAT is present, not WHERE.

cards.title: Why convolution (not dense layers)?
cards.hook: Dense layers forget which pixels were neighbours and need millions of weights.
cards.visual:
Problem with FCConvolution's answer
Flattening destroys 2D neighbourhoodslocal connectivity (3×3 patches)
224×224×3 = 150,528 inputs × 1,000 units = 150,528,000 weightsshared weights: one small filter reused everywhere
Hand-written rules can't cover every variationlearn the features from data
example: Two different '7's share a top bar, a descending diagonal and a lower stroke: local filters can match both.
cards.trap: Hand-engineered features must anticipate viewpoint, illumination, scale, deformation, occlusion, pose, clutter and intra-class variation.

cards.hook: Slide the filter, multiply element-wise, sum: one number per position.
example: Step 1: window rows 0-2, cols 0-2. Matches with +1 weights: 1; with −1 weights: 3 → 1 − 3 = −2.
cards.trap: Floor before +1, and padding counts twice (2P).

cards.title: Filters, channels and parameter counts
cards.src: Lecture 7, slide 40; Key points about convolution filters and parameter counts
cards.hook: Each filter looks through ALL input channels and produces ONE output channel.
example: Two 3×3 filters on RGB with bias: (3×3×3 + 1)×2 = 56.
cards.memory: Filter depth = input depth; output depth = filter count.
cards.trap: Forgetting the bias, or forgetting × C_in.

cards.title: ReLU and pooling
cards.hook: ReLU keeps positive evidence; pooling keeps the strongest response and shrinks the map.

cards.memory: Pooling: keep the loudest voice in each room.
cards.trap: Pooling has NO learnable weights and does not change the number of channels.

cards.title: CNN classifiers, training & classic architectures
cards.hook: Conv + ReLU + pool blocks extract features; a head turns them into class scores.
formula: load pretrained → replace head → small LR → unfreeze selected → evaluate
example: AlexNet 2012 (large kernels, ReLU, dropout, GPU), VGG11 2014 (repeated 3×3), ResNet18 2015 (skip connections).
cards.memory: Spatial size shrinks, channels grow, receptive field grows.
cards.trap: Don't put softmax in the model when training with CrossEntropyLoss: it expects raw logits.
